_README: Expected NORMAL change of an indicator in microgravity, relative to the astronaut's pre-flight baseline. 'shift' and its source come from published in-flight measurements. 'ramp_days' linearly brings the shift from 0 at launch to its full value; where the source does not give the time course, the ramp is a TEAM ASSUMPTION and says so. Measured on the ISS: applying it to partial gravity (Moon, Mars surface) is an extrapolation.

temperature.ramp_basis: Source: the rise of about 1 °C 'developed gradually over 2.5 months'. Linear shape is a team assumption.
temperature.summary: Resting core temperature rises by about 1 °C over the first 2.5 months of flight.
temperature.source: Stahn et al., 'Increased core body temperature in astronauts during long-duration space missions', Scientific Reports 7:16180 (2017). https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5701078/

bp_systolic.ramp_basis: TEAM ASSUMPTION: the source measured once between flight days 85 and 192; a linear onset up to day 85 is assumed.
bp_systolic.summary: 24-h ambulatory systolic pressure is about 8 mmHg lower in flight than before launch.
bp_systolic.source: Norsk et al., 'Fluid shifts, vasodilatation and ambulatory blood pressure reduction during long duration spaceflight', J Physiol 593:573-584 (2015). https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4324706/

bp_diastolic.ramp_basis: TEAM ASSUMPTION: the source measured once between flight days 85 and 192; a linear onset up to day 85 is assumed.
bp_diastolic.summary: 24-h ambulatory diastolic pressure is about 9 mmHg lower in flight than before launch.
bp_diastolic.source: Norsk et al., 'Fluid shifts, vasodilatation and ambulatory blood pressure reduction during long duration spaceflight', J Physiol 593:573-584 (2015). https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4324706/
